title: Development of an Electrochemical DNA Biosensor to Detect a Foodborne Pathogen
protocol: Quickly add 10 mL of sodium citrate solution (38.8 mM) to 100 mL of boiling aqueous chloroauric acid solution (1 mM).
Cool the prepared AuNPs solution down to ambient temperature.
Place PLA pellets in a stainless-steel mold for melting at 190 °C for 10 min.
Press PLA pellets under pressure of 2.2 MPa for 1 min.
Allow the PLA sheet to cool for about 3 h before use.
Stir vigorously to dissolve 0.68 mg of PLA sheets in 5 mL chloroform at room temperature.
Mix the dissolved PLA with 10 mL AuNPs solution and stir homogeneously at room temperature.
Pipette 25 μL of homogeneous PLA-AuNPs solution onto SPCE.
Air dry the modified SPCE for 24 hours prior to use.
Characterize the modified SPCE/PLA-AuNPs using UV-Vis, XRD, TEM, and FESEM with EDX.
Prepare stock solutions of all oligonucleotides at a concentration of 100 µM using sterile TE solution.
Divide the prepared oligonucleotide solutions into analytical portions.
Store these portions at -4°C.
Make appropriate dilutions just before use.
Immobilize 25 μL of thiolated ssDNA probe on SPCE/PLA-AuNPs.
Air dry the surface for 24 hours at room temperature.
Pipette 25 μL of complementary DNA onto the surface of SPCE/PLA-AuNPs/ssDNA.
Carry out hybridization.
Immerse the immobilized and hybridized electrodes in 20 µM MB for 30 min.
Remove non-specifically adsorbed DNA and excess MB by washing with 0.5 M ABS/20 mM NaCl (pH 4.5).
Rinse with deionized water.
Measure the peak current of MB reduction using DPV technique.
Execute the DPV measurement using 0.1 M PBS (pH 7) containing no indicator.
Immerse the SPCE/PLA-AuNPs in 20 µM MB for 30 min.
Wash with 0.5 M ABS/20 mM NaCl (pH 4.5).
Rinse with deionized water prior to measuring.
Measure the electrochemical reduction of probe DNA, complementary DNA, mismatched DNA, and non-complementary DNA samples using DPV technique.
Select bacterial samples based on their significant contamination of seafood.
Sub-culture bacterial strains every two weeks to maintain viability.
Inoculate preserved bacterial cell cultures in glycerol stocks into respective broths.
Incubate broths according to specific growth conditions for each strain.
Maintain long-term preservation at -80 °C with 20% (v/v) glycerol.
Determine the quantity of V. parahaemolyticus cells using a spread plate technique.
Culture Vibrio parahaemolyticus in Trypticase Soy Broth (TSB + 3% NaCl) at 37°C with shaking at 140 rpm.
Transfer 1 mL of the bacterial culture to 9 mL of TSB + 3% NaCl to create a 10-1 dilution.
Repeat the dilution step nine more times to achieve up to a 10-10 dilution factor.
Spread 0.1 mL of each dilution (from 10-1 to 10-10) onto a Vibrio selective agar plate for colony counting.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 24 hours.
Count individual colonies using a colony counter.
Back-calculate CFU/mL density by multiplying the count per pipetted amount by the dilution factor.
Derive the concentration of CFUs in bacterial cell suspensions from the calibration plot of CFU/mL against absorbance.
Streak an individual bacterial strain on agar media and inoculate it into broth media for incubation at its specific growth conditions with shaking at 140 rpm.
Pipette 1 mL of broth culture into a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 4830 x g and 4°C for 1 minute to obtain bacterial pellets.
Resuspend the pellet in about 500 µL of sterile TE buffer.
Heat the suspension at 98 ± 2 °C for 10 minutes in a heating block.
Chill the heated suspension immediately at -18°C for 10 minutes to lyse cells and release DNA.
Centrifuge the genomic DNA at 4830 x g and 4°C for 3 min.
Keep the supernatant at -20°C.
Measure the concentration and purity of the extracted genomic DNA using a biophotometer with UV absorption at wavelengths of 260 nm and 280 nm.
Identify all strains using standard biochemical assays.
Verify strains by 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
Denature the genomic DNA at 92°C for 2 min.
Cool the denatured DNA rapidly in ice water.
Prepare a PCR reaction mixture with sterile water, buffer, primer pair, dNTP mix, DNA template, and Taq DNA polymerase.
Mix all components well.
Program a thermocycler for initial denaturation at 94°C for 3 min.
Cycle through denaturation (94°C, 1 min), annealing (63°C, 1.5 min), and extension (72°C, 1.5 min) for 30 cycles.
Perform a final extension at 72°C for 7 min.
Determine the amplified products and their sizes via electrophoresis on a 1.5% agarose gel.
Capture the gel images with a commercially produced gel-documentation system.
Obtain fresh cockle samples from the wet market.
Divide the samples into treated and untreated groups.
Pre-treat cockles in the treated group by storing them at -20 °C for 24 hours.
Expose pre-treated cockles to UV light at 20 °C for 4 hours prior to DNA extraction.
Analyze samples from the untreated group directly without any pre-treatment.
Subculture V. parahaemolyticus ATCC 17802 in TSB with 3% NaCl.
Determine viable cell levels by plating appropriate dilutions on CA to obtain an inoculum of 10^4 CFU/mL.
Wash cockles in distilled water and scrub off dirt.
Remove tissues from the shell using sterile forceps in a laminar flow cabinet.
Homogenize about 10 g of cockle tissue with 90 mL sterile TSB (3% NaCl) for 60 s.
Add known amount of V. parahaemolyticus to 9 mL of homogenized sample broth for spiked samples.
Use unspiked samples as negative control.
Estimate cell counts by plating 0.1 mL of the spiked and unspiked samples on CA.
Pipette 1 mL of samples into a microcentrifuge tube for DNA extraction.
Extract genomic DNA from spiked and unspiked samples using modified boiled lysis procedure.
Determine DNA concentration and purity using bio photometer measurement at wavelengths of 260 nm and 280 nm.
